issue.title: agent: MiniMax Code 改了「数据目录」后，magpie 仍把 provider 写到 `~/.minimax`，因此桌面版的模型选择器里看不到
issue.body:
# agent: MiniMax Code — magpie doesn't follow the desktop app's moved data folder, so the desktop's model list never changes

> This is #1788 for MiniMax Code: the same bug, another agent. There, ZCode's data folder was moved and magpie kept writing `~/.zcode/v2`; it was fixed in v0.1.1225 by reading the app's own record of the move (`appdir.ZCodeDataIn`). MiniMax Code's desktop app records the same kind of choice, and magpie never reads it.

## Summary

MiniMax Code's desktop app can keep its data folder somewhere other than `~/.minimax`; the user picks the place in the app's settings. magpie does not look for that place: it writes `custom_provider.magpie` into `~/.minimax/config.yaml` whatever the desktop app reads, and reports the agent as wired.

The result is a silent split. magpie's UI shows the model list it just wrote, and the desktop app keeps the list it had. Nothing in magpie says the two disagree.

## What magpie writes, and what the desktop reads

On this machine the desktop app's data folder was moved to `D:\minimax data`, which it records in its own settings:

```console
$ cat "%APPDATA%\MiniMax\minimax-agent-cn-config.json" | jq '.config | {localRuntimeDataParentDir, localRuntimePreviousDataParentDirs}'
{
  "localRuntimeDataParentDir": "D:\\minimax data",
  "localRuntimePreviousDataParentDirs": [ "C:\\Users\\16439" ]
}
```

The runtime's data folder is that parent plus `.minimax`, so the config the desktop app reads is `D:\minimax data\.minimax\config.yaml`. Its own log says so:

```
[LocalRuntime] Launch plan: buildEnv=prod, dataDirMode=source, policy=enabled, clone=disabled
[UtilityRuntime:stdout] V2 Agent cutover bootstrap receipt already completed; skipping legacy collision scan and import
  {"receipt_path":"D:\\minimax data\\.minimax\\v2\\migration\\manifests\\legacy-agent-bootstrap-import-v1.json"}
```

magpie, meanwhile, writes to the old place:

```console
$ magpie ls
  MiniMax Code      magpie/minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash    ~\.minimax\config.yaml
```

Two files, both with a `custom_provider.magpie`, both looking right, neither seeing the other's models. magpie's `Check` for this agent (`internal/agent/minimax.go`) asks whether `defaultModel` in **its** file names `custom_provider:magpie` and whether `custom_provider.magpie` is in **its** file — both true, so the agent reads as wired (`"wired": true` in the state magpie keeps).

## What it looks like

The desktop app's model picker keeps the list from the file it read, and its own `defaultModel` keeps a model id from a catalog magpie has since moved on from:

```
404 magpie knows no model "minimax-cn~MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview";
    did you mean minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, auto/glm-5.3-flash, zhipu/glm-5.3-flash?
```

The desktop app is asking the gateway for a model magpie no longer serves, because the file the desktop app reads was written by a magpie whose catalog was a few models behind. The desktop app's model list is what magpie wrote to a file the desktop app never reads.

## Root cause

**1. MiniMax Code's data folder is found by a fixed path plus one env var.**

`internal/agent/minimax.go`:

```go
// MiniMaxDir is the folder MiniMax Code keeps its config.yaml in.
func MiniMaxDir(home string) string {
	if d := strings.TrimSpace(appdir.Getenv("MINIMAX_DATA_DIR")); d != "" {
		return d
	}
	return filepath.Join(home, ".minimax")
}
```

`MINIMAX_DATA_DIR` is the only way to point magpie elsewhere, and nothing on this machine sets it: the desktop app's move is recorded in its own settings file, and magpie does not read that.

**2. Every other agent with a movable data folder has this in `internal/appdir`.**

`appdir` has `zcode.go`, `claude.go`, `codex.go` and `hermes.go`, each of which reads the app's own record of where the user moved its data:

```go
// internal/appdir/zcode.go
func ZCodeDataIn(home string) string {
	var s struct {
		DataBaseDir any `json:"dataBaseDir"`
	}
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(home, ".zcode", "v2", "setting.json"))
	...
}
```

ZCode's own comment says the choice stays in `setting.json` as `dataBaseDir`; magpie reads it, and `magpie ls` shows ZCode's real path (`D:\zcode data\.zcode\v2\config.json` on this machine). MiniMax Code's desktop app records the same kind of choice — in `%APPDATA%\MiniMax\minimax-agent-cn-config.json`, as `config.localRuntimeDataParentDir` — and there is no `internal/appdir/minimax.go` to read it.

**3. The lookup is duplicated, so the fix has two callers.**

The same path is resolved twice, in two packages:

- `internal/agent.MiniMaxDir` — the config file magpie writes the provider into
- `internal/sessions.MiniMaxDir` — where magpie looks for MiniMax Code's sessions

Both are the `MINIMAX_DATA_DIR`-or-`~/.minimax` lookup. As in #1788, one `appdir` helper should serve both.

## Expected

magpie should find MiniMax Code's data folder the way it finds the other agents': read the app's own record of where the user moved it, and use that folder for `config.yaml`.

- Add `appdir.MiniMaxDirIn(home)`: read `config.localRuntimeDataParentDir` from `%APPDATA%\MiniMax\minimax-agent-cn-config.json` (the file the CN build writes), and use `<that>\.minimax` as the data folder. `config.localRuntimePreviousDataParentDirs` lists the parents it was moved away from, so it is the fallback when the app is not installed or has never been moved.
- Use it in `internal/agent/minimax.go`'s `MiniMaxDir` and in `internal/sessions.MiniMaxDir`, as `ZCodeDataIn` is used in #1788.
- `MINIMAX_DATA_DIR` stays the override, as it is for the others.

A user who has moved MiniMax Code's data should not have to know about an env var to have magpie reach the desktop app.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| magpie | 0.1.1294 |
| MiniMax Code desktop | 3.1.3-inside.117 (`com.minimax.agent.cn`, Windows) |
| OS | Windows 11 (10.0.26200 x64) |
| agent | `minimax-code` |
| desktop's data folder | `D:\minimax data\.minimax` (moved from `C:\Users\16439\.minimax`) |

The split was found with `magpie ls` (its path for MiniMax Code) against the desktop app's `minimax-agent-cn-config.json` and its runtime log; the 404 above is the desktop app's own log.

## Workaround

Set `MINIMAX_DATA_DIR` to the folder holding `config.yaml` (`D:\minimax data\.minimax` here) and restart magpie, which then writes the desktop app's file:

```console
$ setx MINIMAX_DATA_DIR "D:\minimax data\.minimax"
```

## Related

- #1788 ZCode 改了「数据目录」后，magpie 仍把 provider 写到 `~/.zcode/v2` —— 同一个 bug，修在 v0.1.1225
- #1286 Plugin models: limit.input replaces the real context window, halving a 1M model to 512k
- #2214 provider: MiniMax M3.1 Flash officially supports both 512K and 1M windows

comments.body:
Fixed on `fix/r25-minimax-moved-data` (fork `skygunner/magpie`, head `4cad21e120deced2560e904f8b9ba845a471e3c9`, one commit on top of `19253f67`): magpie now reads the desktop app's own record of the move and reaches the file the app reads.

**What changed.** `appdir.MiniMaxDirIn` reads `config.localRuntimeDataParentDir` from `%APPDATA%/MiniMax/minimax-agent-cn-config.json` and appends `.minimax`. `internal/agent.MiniMaxDir` (config.yaml) and `internal/sessions.MiniMaxDir` (sessions) both resolve through it, and the library's skills follow the resolved agent dir. `MINIMAX_DATA_DIR` stays the override. A missing, unreadable, malformed, blank or relative record keeps `~/.minimax`, so the old behavior survives anything magpie can't trust.

**Proof.** A new public-API test (`TestMiniMaxDirDesktopRecord`) drives both callers against the same genuine settings file - 14 cases covering the moved parent, whitespace, override precedence, missing/malformed/wrong-typed records and relative/missing APPDATA:

- RED on a pristine `git archive` of base `19253f67` (only the test added): both callers returned `~/.minimax`, exit 1, compile clean.
- GREEN after the fix: 14/14, exit 0.
- `go test -race -shuffle=on -count=1 ./internal/{agent,appdir,sessions,library}` all ok.
- `gofmt`, `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`, native/Linux-nogui/Windows builds all clean.
- Real `magpie ls` in a sandbox HOME with the reporter's settings shape shows `~/minimax data/.minimax/config.yaml`.

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` exits 1 in `internal/{edit,gateway,plugin,provider,testenv}`; the same failures reproduce on a clean base archive, so they are pre-existing and untouched by this change.

**Not verified.** No Windows desktop runtime here, so the desktop-side end-to-end is not re-run; the Windows work was a cross-build and vet only. Only the CN build's settings file is read - other builds keep `~/.minimax` unless they set the env var. Previous data parents are not chased; the current parent determines the active directory.

Source: [shared resolver](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/4cad21e120deced2560e904f8b9ba845a471e3c9/internal/appdir/minimax.go), [public regression test](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/4cad21e120deced2560e904f8b9ba845a471e3c9/internal/agent/minimax_dir_test.go). Raw RED/GREEN, race, vet/build, CLI and baseline logs are retained locally at `/home/vincenty/Projects/magpie-issues/evidence/r25-2998/`; these logs are not published in the fork. The commit message’s docs/fork evidence path is inaccurate; this is the correct location.
